chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when a matter that pleased him reached him, would say: 'All praise is due to Allah for this favor.' And when a matter that grieved him reached him, he would say: 'All praise is due to Allah in every state.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say when pleased or grieved by a matter?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on gratitude, this hadith distinguishes between specific thanksgiving for blessings and the profound, all-encompassing contentment (rida) with divine decree during hardship. It reflects the Shia theological emphasis on maintaining spiritual equilibrium, where the believer acknowledges Allah’s wisdom in both ease and difficulty, viewing every state as a distinct manifestation of mercy.
